deities: Ibudhou Thangjing (Thangching) - guardian and supreme deity of Moirang, progenitor of the Moirang dynasty, associated with righteousness and Loktak Lake
festivals: Thangjing Lai Haraoba - annual festival in the Meitei lunar month of Kalen (early summer; travel sources give May, lasting about a week, with Khamba-Thoibi dance, singing and feasting; one source says 'about a month' - verify)

history.dynasty: Moirang dynasty of Ancient Manipur by legend (royal attires of 12th-century Moirang kings preserved and displayed at the temple)
history.period: Ancient - traditionally millennia old, closely tied to the Khamba-Thoibi epic; exact founding date undocumented (verify)
history.summary: IDENTITY CONFIRMED: the Ibudhou Thangjing Temple is the primary seat of worship for Thangjing (Thangching) at Moirang town, Bishnupur district, Manipur, very close to the banks of Loktak Lake - a traditional Sanamahi (Meitei indigenous religion) shrine, NOT a conventional Hindu temple, and one of the most culturally vital Meitei pilgrimage sites. Legend holds that the classical Khamba Thoibi Jagoi dance was first performed at this temple by Khuman Khamba and Moirang Thoibi during the Lei Langba ritual, and the temple preserves/displays the royal attires of 12th-century Moirang kings. Must not be conflated with the separate hilltop shrine of Ibudhou Thangjing at Thangjing Hill (Churachandpur district), to which the annual Meitei pilgrimage climbs each April. FLAGS: (1) founding date undocumented - traditional/legendary antiquity only, verify; (2) festival duration conflict: sources say the Lai Haraoba lasts about a week (Wikipedia) vs 'about a month' (travel sites) - verify; (3) CSV 'state' column held the town name (Moirang) - real state is Manipur; (4) coordinates are Moirang-town level (24.49721, 93.76521), near Loktak Lake - temple-level precision not available; (5) media empty - no shrine-specific image found after genuine search attempts (image results were the Kangla Pakhangba temple and the Nongmaiching Sanamahi temple, not this shrine).

name: Ibudhou Thangjing Temple, Moirang
town_description: Moirang is a small town in Bishnupur district, Manipur, on the southern shore of Loktak Lake, about 45 km from Imphal. It is the traditional centre of Meitei culture - seat of the ancient Moirang dynasty and the Khamba-Thoibi legend - and a major tourist stop for the Ibudhou Thangjing Temple, the INA Museum (where the tricolour was first hoisted on Indian soil in April 1944), and nearby Sendra Island and Keibul Lamjao National Park.
